title: Reaction-Time Decline Under Heavy Caffeine
dataSources: Continuous glucose (`cgm:glucose`), HRV (`hrv:reading`), mood check-ins (`mood:checkin`), ketone readings (`ketone:reading`), reaction-time trials (`reaction:trial`), sauna sessions (`sauna:session`), resting temperature (`temp:reading`), and meditation logs (`meditation:session`).
app: Biohacking telemetry from CGMs, HRV devices, ketone meters, mood and meditation journals, reaction-time apps, sauna logs, and health sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=reaction:trial
| stats avg(reaction_ms) as avg_reaction_ms by caffeine_bucket_mg
| sort caffeine_bucket_mg
description: Compares reaction time across caffeine buckets so overstimulation becomes as visible as under-caffeination.
value: More caffeine is not always better, and a reaction-time view helps find the point where focus begins to worsen.
implementation: Pair reaction-time trials with the most recent caffeine estimate and bucket those totals into practical ranges.
visualization: Line chart of average reaction time by caffeine bucket.
grandmaExplanation: It maps whether lots of caffeine is actually helping your reflexes or starting to make them worse.
